opportunity: kuna's built-in prototype tables share one width-stable type vocabulary, so all 108 aggregate-pointer slots in them are spelled `void *`. `void *` never matches a ground-truth `FILE *` (the metric's width-only generosity has no pointer entry), and named-struct pointers are 22.5% of matchable GT variables -- a class kuna scores 0.0% on while ida scores 432 / ghidra 382 / binja 523 TP on the same 92-binary sample. The libc/POSIX-namable slice of it is ~4.1% of matchable GT (FILE 605 occurrences, stat 255, passwd 136).
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-libctypes.xml (6 two-pass assertions over a real ELF via `load file`) + 10 table-invariant unit tests in analyzers::protos::kuna_libctypes::tests
inspiration: Ghidra ApplyDataArchiveAnalyzer applying generic_clib_64.gdt, whose FILE */struct stat * slots carry the header's own pointee; signatures reduced from `gcc -aux-info` over the platform headers (_GNU_SOURCE + _FORTIFY_SOURCE=2); widths from sizeof/_Alignof

table.held_name_rule: a name already held is adopted only when it is a struct that is either INCOMPLETE (our own shell, or a DWARF forward declaration) or COMPLETE at the declared width (the platform's own definition on a -g binary); a complete struct of a different width is a program's own type sharing the spelling, and the whole signature is declined rather than pointed at it.
table.width_abi: glibc x86-64 (sizeof/_Alignof). On another ABI a width can be a few bytes off, which can only change whether an access renders as a field or as a cast; the name is ABI-independent and a wrong width cannot make a pointer point at the wrong thing.

selection_rule: a retarget restates a shipped signature with the same arity and variadic slot, so it needs no new evidence; a NEW name needs a machine-readable declaration (`gcc -aux-info`) AND corpus weight, measured as PLT call sites over the 524 stripped O0+O2 decbench ELFs. Kept: rewind 117, __uflow 77, fgetc 57, freopen 32, funlockfile 20, getdelim 18, flockfile 18, popen 17, pclose 17. Rejected: fgetc_unlocked 0, fmemopen 0, __underflow 0 (and no installed declaration to reduce).

corpus_sweep.method: `kuna decompile-all` off vs opaque over 7 binaries (fmt/ls/grep/gzip/tar O2, find/diff O0), every changed line classified plus a control-flow/call/constant skeleton comparison per function; raw output in corpus-hunk-classification.txt
corpus_sweep.classification: every inspected skeleton difference is an offset constant becoming a field name or an `&` replacing a cast; two representative cases are improvements (diffutils 0x10e15 collapses 20 scattered stack slots into one on-stack struct sigaction; gzip 0x65d0 types the localtime result `tm *`). No wrong-output hunk found.

notes: The gate is read INSIDE the pass through the load-time env bridge, not at the commit boundary: the pass interns its named shells into the type factory while building the signatures, and a commit-boundary arch flag additionally drops facts after `clear architecture` + `load file` (measured -- it made pass 2 of the stage test render `fclose(void *)`). stdin/stdout/stderr as typed FILE * data symbols, and a `glibc` value installing the public _IO_FILE field names, are follow-ups.

default_decision.verdict: ship default-OFF in this PR; the flip is a separate PR (campaign Stage 3)
default_decision.evidence_for_on: typesweep 214 slices / 5298 functions: +39 perfect, 0 moved off perfect, 386 improved, 0 worsened; make test 675/675 PARITY OK with the gate forced on (KUNA_LIBCTYPES=opaque); make test-stages 1013/1013 PARITY OK with the gate forced on; whole-binary sweep over 7 binaries shows no wrong-output hunk and no change in the PTRSUB( count; speed flat (see speed).
default_decision.blocker: `make test-cli` goes 169/170 with the gate forced on: the promoted probe tests/cli/changing-namestyle-invalidates-discovered.json pins `sub_1249(void *param_1)` on decompiler/crates/kuna-analysis/tests/fixtures/stripped_dynamic_x86_64, and that parameter becomes `FILE *`. The new spelling is CORRECT -- the body is fclose(param_1) / fread(...,param_1) -- but rewriting another feature's regression probe belongs in the flip PR with that justification, not in the PR that introduces the option.

speed.method: interleaved off/opaque pairs through the load-time env bridge (`kuna decompile-all --option libctypes off|opaque`), MINIMUM and median of 15 pairs each, alternating which arm runs first; the MINIMUM is the honest read because the box was shared with a concurrent gate run

rows.case: fmt functions (load + the whole pass list, no body decompiled)

speed.why: the load-time cost is ~20 `get_type_struct`/`find_by_name` calls (the `fmt functions` row, +0.08% on the minimum, is that cost in isolation). The whole-binary rows carry the real cost: a named 216-byte pointee participates in type propagation where a `void *` did not. The `fmt functions` median (+14.92% against a +0.08% minimum) and the `ls` median are contention from a concurrent gate run, not signal.

ablation_evidence: `kuna decompile-all` over the whole O2/coreutils/stripped/fmt: this branch with `--option libctypes off` is byte-identical to the main tree's own build (0 of 4,069 lines differ).
